extraction_notes: QUBT FY2021 10-K reports $0 revenue (pre-revenue dev-stage). No specific Pentagon Program Elements (PE numbers) or named DoD programs (e.g., AFRL Quantum Networking, SDA Tracking Layer, Skyborg) are disclosed. Government-funding language is generic and points to NQIA / NIST / NSF / DOE civilian/intelligence sectors, not Pentagon line items. Per blinded protocol, claims still extracted and probed; J-Book queries are expected to return NOT_FOUND or UNVERIFIABLE because the company never names a PE. The cohort pattern (J-Book divergence) only fires when a specific program is named — its absence here is itself a finding (no concrete forward DoD-program revenue narrative to test). Subsidiary references at cutoff: QPhoton, Inc. (then in exclusivity/LOI; not yet closed); QI Solutions and Qubittech not mentioned in this filing.

claims.claim_text: QCI is pursuing US Government opportunities under the National Quantum Initiative Act (NQIA), which authorizes NIST, NSF, and DOE to fund quantum research, including a FY2020 DOE initiative of $625 million over five years to establish two to five multidisciplinary QIS Research Centers.
claims.subject: Quantum Computing Inc.
claims.object_value: NQIA / NIST / NSF / DOE quantum R&D programs
claims.source_quote: the Company is pursuing a number of US government funded opportunities. The US Government, through the National Quantum Initiative Act of 2018 ... authorizes the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), the National Science Foundation (NSF), and the Department of Energy (DOE), to strengthen QIS Programs ... a fiscal year 2020 Department of Energy initiative of $625 million over the next five years to establish two to five multidisciplinary Quantum Information Science (QIS) Research Centers

claims.claim_text: QCI is a founding member of the Quantum Economic Development Consortium (QED-C), established with support from NIST as part of the Federal QIS strategy.
claims.subject: Quantum Computing Inc.
claims.source_quote: The Quantum Economic Development Consortium (QED-C) ... was established with support from the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) as part of the Federal strategy for advancing quantum information science. The Company is one of the founding members of the QED-C.

claims.claim_text: QCI has entered a Technology Alliance Partnership Agreement with Splunk to pursue government-funded research on cybersecurity analytics, network security, dynamic logistics and scheduling using QCI's Qatalyst platform.
claims.subject: Quantum Computing Inc.
claims.source_quote: the Company has entered into a Technology Alliance Partnership agreement with Splunk, Inc. (NASDAQ: SPLK). The Company is partnering with Splunk to pursue government funded efforts to do both fundamental and applied research and develop analytics ... The initial efforts of our partnership with Splunk will focus on three key challenges; network security, dynamic logistics and scheduling.

claims.claim_text: QCI's Qatalyst quantum software is integrated with Amazon Braket and offers access to D-Wave, Rigetti, IonQ, and IBM quantum processing units.
claims.subject: Qatalyst (QCI product)
claims.object_value: Amazon Braket, D-Wave, Rigetti, IonQ, IBM
claims.source_quote: Qatalyst is integrated with the Amazon Cloud BRAKET API, offering access to multiple Quantum Processing Units (QPUs) including DWave, Rigetti, and IonQ. Qatalyst also integrates directly with IBM s QPUs.
